Creation of a Gene Bank 
*322. SHRIMATI VANGA GEETHA: Will the Minister of SCIENCE 
AND TECHNOLOGY be pleased to state: 
(a) whether Government have any proposal to create a gene bank for 
private and public organisations; 
(b) if so, the modalities worked out in this regard so far; and 
(c) the funds allocated for the current Five Year Plan for this purpose? 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SCIENCE AND 
TECHNOLOGY (SHRI KAPIL SIBAL): (a) to (c) A Statement is laid on the 
Table of the House. 
Statement 
(a) and (b) Yes, Sir. The Government has already established National 
Gene Banks for Microbes, Blue Gr een Algae, Marine Cyanobacteria, 
Medicinal & Aromatic Plants, Drosophiia, Filarial Parasites, Seeds for food 
and agricultural crops, etc. These Gene Banks which are being supported by the 
Ministry of Science and Technology, (Department of Biotechnology, Council 
of Scientific and Industrial Research) and Indian Council of Agricultural 
Research, are accessible to public and private sector organizations for utilizing 
the genetic material as per their requirement. Setting up of more gene 
banks/repositories would depend upon the needs and requirements of scientists, 
institutions and industry engaged in research, production and trade. 
(c) A total amount of Rs. 46.28 Crores has been allocated for the current 
five year plan for these Gene Banks, where Department of Biotechnology, 
Council of Scientific and Industrial Research and Indian Council of 
Agricultural Research have allocated Rs. 15.84, Rs. 4.00 and Rs. 26.44 Crores 
respectively. 
SHRIMATI VANGA GEETHA: Sir, the technology, more particularly 
bio-technology, scientific and industrial research, apart from agricultural 
research are very essential for all round development of our country; and to 
compete with the developed countries we  need to encourage our research and 
scientific fraternity to achieve our goals. In this background, I would like to 
know from the hon. Minister how far the gene banks established in our 
country are useful for the scientists and the common man of our country? Is 
there any intellectual audit in various scientific organisations of our country? 
If so, what are the details?

SHRI KAPIL SIBAL: Mr. Chairman, Sir, I think, it is the obligation of 
every country to, in fact, establish gene banks to protect its bio-diversity. With 
that in mind we have established gene  banks in various areas from medicinal 
and aromatic plants to seeds in agricultural produce to blue and green algae, 
cyanobacteria, a range of things to prot ect our biodiversity. In fact, we have 
one international depository authority as well, which is Institute of Molecular 
Technology, IMTECH, which is situated in Chandigarh, which accords to 
international standards. In the Ministry of Agriculture, we have, in fact 
accessions of 3,00,000, which is probably the largest in Asia. So, we are taking 
care of our gene banks. We need to make much better efforts at this and we have, 
in fact, written to the various Departments of Government of India under various 
Ministries to establish international depository authorities. Certainly, audits are 
taking place. Basically a gene bank is a service agency. So, we are servicing all 
in the private sector and the public sect or; whenever they want any particular 
micro-organism, we supply to them and that really is the basic purpose of a 
gene bank.

they

Statement 
(a) For assisting eligible applicants in setting up agro and rural 
industries, the Central Government implements the Rural Employment 
Generation Programme (REGP) and Prime Minister's Rozgar Yojana 
(PMRY). Under both these programmes, loans are provided to eligible 
applicants by banks and subsidy by the Government. The State/Union 
Territory (UT)-wise details of investment made under REGP and PMRY 
during 2002-03, 2003-04, 2004-05 and 2005-06 (upto September 2005) 
are given in the enclosed Statement-I and Statement-ll, respectively, (See 
below). 
(b) The problems of agro and rural industries include use of obsolete 
technology, inconsistent quality of products, products not being in tune with 
the market demand, inadequate and delayed credit, management deficiencies, 
etc. 
(c) The primary responsibility of promoting small scale industries (SSI), 
including agro and rural industries, re sts with the State/LIT Governments. 
However, the Central Government implements a number of schemes to 
supplement the efforts of the State/UT Government. Some of the important 
schemes are: 
(i) Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme (CLCSS) for technology 
upgradation and modernisation of production techniques; 
(ii) Small Industry Cluster Development Programme (SICDP) for 
holistic development of SSI clusters; 
(iii) Credit Guarantee Fund Scheme for Small Industries for providing 
guarantee cover to banks for collateral-free loans upto Rs. 25 lakh; 
(iv) Rural Industries Service Cent res (RISC) Scheme for setting up of 
common facility centres (CFCs) to provide infrastructural support 
and services to such industries; 
(v) Product Development, Design Intervention and Packaging (PRODIP) 
Scheme for improved design and packaging of village industry 
products; 
(vi) Financial assistance to village industry units for participation in 
national and international level exhibitions for market development;

RAJYA SABHA [15 December, 2005] 
Statement 
(a) The latest information on State-wise teledensity (rural and urban areas) i.e. upto 
31.10.2005 is given in the enclosed Statement-I (See below). 
(b) and (c) Yes Sir. The rural teledensity has been lower than the urban tele-density 
because the development of network was more urban centric, particularly in the Private 
Sector. Higher economic and literacy status in the urban areas were also contributing 
factors. 
(d) A number of steps have been taken by the Government to increase the 
telephone density in rural areas which include the following: 
(i) Setting up of the USO Fund by the Government for provision of telephones 
in the rural areas; 
(ii) Bharat Sanchar Nigam Limited (BSNL) has relaxed the distance for laying 
outdoor cables from 2.5 Kms. to 5 Kms. for Landline Exchanges which would facilitate 
larger coverage in the rural areas from existing exchanges; and 
(iii) Increased provision of WLL (Wireless in Local Loop) phones by BSNL.

*327. SHRI MANOJ BHATTACHARYA: Will the PRIME MINISTER 
be pleased to state:

Statement 
(a) to (c) The July 18,2005 understanding on India-US civil nuclear 
energy cooperation agreed by India and the United States of America. The 
elements of this understanding as contained in the Joint Statement are as 
follows:— 
* President Bush conveyed his appreciation to the Prime Minister over 
India's strong commitment to preventing WMD proliferation and stated 
that as a responsible state with advanced nuclear technology, India 
should acquire the same benefits and advantages as other such States. The 
US President told the Prime Minister that he would work to achieve full 
civil nuclear energy cooperation with India as it realizes its goals of 
promoting nuclear power and achieving energy security. 
* The US President would also seek agreement from the US Congress to adjust 
U.S. laws and policies, and the United States will work with friends and 
allies to adjust international regimes to enable full civil nuclear energy 
cooperation and trade with India, including but 
31 

RAJYA SABHA [15 December, 2005] 
not limited to expenditious consideration of fuel supplies for 
safeguarded nuclear reactors at Tara pur. In the meantime, the United 
States will encourage its partners to also consider this request expeditiously. 
* India has expressed its interest in ITER and a willingness to contribute. 
The United States will consult with its partners considering India's 
participation. 
* The United States will consult with the other participants in the 
Generation IV International Forum with a view towards India's 
inclusion. 
* The Prime Minister conveyed that for its part, India would reciprocally 
agree that it would be ready to assume the same responsbilities and 
practices and acquire the same benefits and advantages as other leading 
countries with advanced nuclear technology, such as the United States. 
These responsibilities and practices consist of: 
 
■ identifying and separating civilian and military nuclear facilities and 
programmes in a phased manner and filing a declaration regarding its 
civilian facilities with the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA); 
■ taking a decision to place voluntarily its civilian nuclear facilities 
under IAEA safeguards; signing a nd adhering to an Additional 
Protocol with respect to civilian nuclear facilities; 
■ continuing India's unilateral moratorium on nuclear testing; working 
with the United States for the conclusion of a multilateral Fissile 
Material Cut Off Treaty; 
■ refraining from transfer of enrichment and reprocessing 
technologies to States that do not have them and supporting 
international efforts to limit their spread; and 
■ ensuring that the necessary steps ha ve been taken to secure nuclear 
materials and technology through comprehensive export control 
legislation and through harmonization and adherence to Missile 
Technology Control Regime (MTCR) and Nuclear Suppliers Group 
(NSG) guidelines. 
The implementation of the July 18 understanding would be guided fully 
and entirely by the commitments reflected in the Joint Statement

THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE MINISTRY OF SCIENCE AND 
TECHNOLOGY (SHRI KAPIL SIBAL): (a) The earthquake of 8th October, 
2005 (occurred in Pakistan near Muzaffarabad), as referred to in the question, 
was widely felt in parts of northern States like Jammu and Kashmir (J&K), 
Punjab, Himachal Pradesh, Delhi and Ra jasthan, etc. As per the information 
provided by Ministry of Home Affairs, a total number of 1,338 persons have 
lost their lives (1336 it) Jammu and Kashmir and 2 in Punjab). Over 39,000 
buildings/houses are reported to have been fully-damaged, while more than 
71,000 were reported to be partially damaged in the State of J&K. 
(b) As per the seismic zoning map published by Bureau of Indian 
Standard (BIS), the country has been divided into four seismic zones, 
namely, zone-ll-V. Zone-V is consider ed to be more seismically active, 
while zone-ll is the least. Accordingly to this classification, Delhi falls in 
zone-IV which can experience earthquake of intensity up to VIII on 
Modified Mercalli (MM) scale. The intensity at a given place depends on 
the magnitude and distance of the ear thquake epicenter. Delhi can be 
affected by strong earthquakes occurring in the highly earthquake prone 
regions in Himalaya besides local earthquakes of small to moderate 
magnitudes. As per intensity VIII of MM scale the maximum damage that 
can occur to structures in Delhi due to earthquakes is as follows:. 
(i) Slight in specially designed structures 
(ii)        Considerable in ordinary buildings 
(iii)       Very heavy in poorly built structures 
A study of microzonation of Delhi has recently been completed at 
1:50,000 scale, which shows that within the city of Delhi itself the impact of an 
earthquake may not be uniform over the city due to varying properties of the soil and 
geological characteristics. However, at this stage it is difficult to say how safe is 
Delhi from earthquakes. 
(c) to (e) Based on the present st andards prescribed by BIS, the

and Country Planning Legislation, Zoning Regulation Development Control 
and Building Regulation/Bye-laws for Safety against earthquakes have been 
prepared by an Expert Committee constituted by the Ministry of Home Affairs,

to meet the requirements of the States. Microzonation of urban areas may lead to

Uranium Deposits 
2426. SHRIMATI S. G. INDIRA: Will the PRIME MINISTER be 
pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that India has tied up the medium term fuel 
supplies for nuclear energy programme of generating 13,000 m.w. of power; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether it is also a fact that country is developing Indigenous air borne 
survey instruments to locate more deposits of Uranium; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE PRIME MINISTERS OFFICE 
(SHRI PRITHVIRAJ CHAV AN): (a) and (b) Present nuclear programme 
envisages reaching 13000 MWe generation capacity by 2013. We expect this 
capacity to be made up of a mix of Pressurised Heavy Water Reactors (PHWRs), 
Light Water Reactors (LWRs) and Fast Breeder Reactors (FBRs). While fuel 
for PHWRs would be supplied from indigenous mines, fuel for LWRs would 
need to be imported. FBR would run on recycled fuel materials. 
(c) Yes, Sir. 
(d) India is developing Air Borne Survey instruments indigenously to 
locate more deposits of Uranium. The development is done jointly by various 
constituent R&D Units and PSU of this Department as well as other 
institutions. The system being developed is called Airborne Time Domain 
Electromagnetic Survey System with a ca pability to identify the presence of 
uranium deposits located below ground level.

operators in 2003; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof and the action plan of Government to 
reserve the trend? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF 
COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (DR. 
SHAKEEL AHMAD): (a) and (b) The rural tele-density as on March 1999 was 
0.52 as compared to urban tele-density of 2.3. As on 30th September, 2005 the 
rural tele-density has increased to 1.77 as compared to urban tele-density of 
31.25. This is happening because the Telecom service providers (especially 
those in the private sector) are focusing more on urban areas because of higher 
revenue per line in urban areas as compared to that in rural areas. 
(c) and (d) The rural tele-density as on March 2003 was 1.49 as 
compared to urban tele-density of 14.32, whereas as on 30th September 2005 the 
rural tele-density has increased to 1.77 as compared to urban tele-density of 
31.25. 
To provide support for expansion of telegraph services Universal Service 
Obligation Fund (USOF) has been created w.e.f. 1.4.2002. Some of the activities 
for which support from USOF has been extended include: 
(i) Provision of Village Public Telephones (VPTs) in 66,822 
remaining unconnected villages excluding villages having 
population less than 100, lying in thick forest area/naxalite infested 
areas etc. by November 2007.14,233 VPTs have been provided as on 
31.10.2005. 
(ii) Provision of second VPT in the form of Rural Community Phones 
(RCPs) in villages having population of more than 2,000 and having no 
PCQ by September 2007. 15,946 RCPs have been provided as on 
30.09.2005. 
(iii) To provide Rural Phone Connectivity 'on demand' in 1,685 
commercially unviable Short Distance Charging Areas (SDCAs) by 
the first quarter of the year 2006.

Assessment of poverty line 
+2523. DR. PRABHA THAKUR: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to 
state: 
(a) the criteria for assessing a person or a family in the country 
living Below Poverty Line; 
 
(b) whether this assessment is done every year and in what way 
common people are informed about it; 
(c) whether any increase or decrease has been taking place every year in terms of 
the number of people living Below Poverty Line in the State of Rajasthan; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof, district-wise? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING (SHRI M. 
V. RAJASEKHARAN): (a) Planning Commission uses per capita 
† Original notice of the question was received in Hindi. 
161 

RAJYA SABHA [15 December, 2005] 
consumption expenditure as the criterion for assessing a person living below 
poverty line in the country. This assessment is done for individuals and not for 
families. The Task Force on 'Minimum Needs and Effective Consumption 
Demands' (1979) fixed the per capita consumption norm at Rs. 49.09 per 
month in rural areas and Rs. 56.64 per month in urban areas at 1973-74 prices 
at national level, corresponding to a basket of goods and services anchored on 
a norm of per capita daily calorie requirement of 2400 kcal. in rural areas and 
2100 kcal. in urban areas, which also meets a minimum of non-food 
requirements, such as clothing, shelter, transport etc. The Task Force used the 
age-sex-activity specific calorie allowances recommended by the Nutrition 
Expert Group (1968) to estimate the average daily per capita requirement for 
rural and urban areas using the age-sex-occupational structure of their 
respective population (as projected for 1982-83). The per capita consumption 
expenditure fixed for State/UT for determination of the poverty line are 
derived from the national level per capita consumption expenditure, using State-
specific price indices and inter-State price differentials, according to the 
methodology given by Expert Group on 'Estimation of Proportion and Number 
of Poor' (Lakdawala Committee 1997). The prescribed per capita consumption 
expenditure limits for determination of people living below poverty line are 
updated using State-specific cost of living indices, that is, Consumer Price 
Indices for Agricultural Labourers (CPIAL) for rural areas and Consumer 
Price Indices for Industrial Workers (CPIIW) for urban areas. 
(b) Planning Commission's assessment on incidence of poverty, that is, 
estimates on percentage of population living below poverty line, at national 
and State level are based on the large sample survey on household consumer 
expenditure conducted by the National Sample Survey Organisation (NSSO) 
at an interval of approximately five years. The latest estimates on population 
living below poverty line are available for the year 1999-2000 (NSS-55th 
Round). These estimates are made available to the public through press 
releases.

2542. SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD: W ill the Minister of SHIPPING, 
ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be pleased to state :

fatal accidents involving Indian Seamen abroad foreign ships;

flag vessels who are being exploited by fly-by night shiplines;

HIGHWAYS (SHRI T.R. BAALU): (a) Yes, Sir.

estimated to be around 50,000. Indian Maritime Administration is not 
controlling employment of Indian seafarers on foreign flag vessels.

Conventions etc. as applicable to the flag country. However, the Director

welfare of Indian seafarers on board foreig n flag ships. It may be difficult to

(b) The Comprehensive Policy for the Maritime Sectors (Ports, 
Merchant Shipping and IWT), which is at draft stage, seeks to combine vision 
and strategy for the sector through harmonious and coordinated development of 
country's maritime assets like ports, shipping, inland water transport systems and 
ship building and ship repair industries. The main points in the draft Policy are 
as follows*:— 
(i) Holistic development of maritime transport systems through a 
coordinated plan and strategies for development of port 
infrastructure, improvement in shipping, backward integration of the 
hinterland through rail, road and inland water transport 
connectivity, augmentation of ship building and ship repair 
facilities so as to emerge as an internationally competitive nation 
in this area by 2025.

(ii) Ensure quality service comparab le with international benchmarks 
in Indian port through modernization, improvement in 
productivity and structural reforms. 
(iii) Facilitate transhipment of Indian origin/bound cargo in Indian 
ports. 
(iv) Effect significant increase in Indian Shipping and IWT tonnage 
through facilitative policy interventions. 
(v) Promote coastal shipping and inland water transport through a 
package of measures including fiscal and financial incentives. 
(vi) Strengthen maritime administration and bring about regulatory 
framework reforms to promote good governance. 
(vii) Provide level playing field to Indian stakeholders by providing 
fiscal regime at par with intern ational norms and by rationalizing 
domestic levies. 
(viii) Provide for state- of-the-art aids to navigation and requisite 
regulatory framework. 
(ix) Encourage ship-building and sh ip-repair activities to become 
internationally competitive a nd emerge as a leading ship-
butkJing/fthip-repair nation by 2025. 
(x) Support ship-breaking and ship-recycling activities without 
compromising on environmental concerns. 
(xi) Stimulate private sector investment including foreign direct 
investment particularly for rendering services of a commercial 
nature in the Maritime sector, by providing conducive 
environment. 
(xii) Promote shipping-trade interface by evolving code of conduct for 
supply chain players such as freight forwarders, shipping agents, 
multimodal transport operators and other intermediaries. 
(xiii) Develop human resources in maritime sector and market them in the 
context of emerging global shortage of qualified personnel in the 
sector.

Credit delivery to SSI 
2563. DR. T SUBBARAMI REDDY: 
SHRI V. HANUMANTHA RAO: 
Will the Minister of SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether better credit delivery to Small Scale Industry sector by RBI, 
State Financing Corporations and SIDBI are necessary for further enhancing 
role of small and medium enterprises; 
(b) whether in its report on national strategy for manufacturing 
National Manufacturing Competitiveness Council (NMCC) has 
recommended that a separate law for small enterprises including chapter on 
provisions of credit to SSIs be framed as prevalent in other countries; 
(c) whether some problems are being faced in accessing credit; and 
(d) if so, what steps considered by Government to remove such- 
hurdles that are being faced by SSI units? 
THE MINISTER OF SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES (SHRI MAHABIR 
PRASAD): (a) Yes, Sir. However, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) does not 
provide credit to the small scale industries (SSI) sector but formulates general 
policies for delivery of credit to the sector by banks, etc. 
209 

RAJYA SABHA [15 December, 2005] 
(b) In its draft report on 'National Strategy for Manufacturing'. The 
National Manufacturing Competitiveness Council has recommended a 
separate law for small enterprises and made several observations on 
provision of credit to the SSI. 
(c) and (d) To facilitate flow of credit to the SSI units, the Government and 
the RBI have taken various measures which, inter alia include enhancement 
in composite loan limit from Rs. 50 lakh to Rs. 1 crore, raising of project cost 
limit under National Equity Fund (NEF) scheme from Rs. 25 lakh to Rs. 50 
lakh, enhancement of eligible loan limit under 
-Credit Guarantee Scheme from Rs. 10 lakh to Rs. 25 lakh, providing 
collaterial free loan upto Rs. 25 lakh to SSI units having good track record, setting 
up of Small and Medium Enterprises (SME) fund of Rs. 10,000 crore under 
Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI), enhancement of credit 
limit under Laghu Udhyami Credit Card (LUCC) from Rs. 2 lakh to Rs. 10 
lakh based on satisfactory track record, etc. 
Further, the Government has announced a 'Policy Package for Stepping 
up Credit to Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs)' on 10th August 2005. 
The measures in the Policy Package to increase the quantum of credit to SMEs 
(including SSIs) include: (i) public sector banks to fix their own targets for 
funding SMEs in order to achieve a minimum 20 per cent year-on-year growth 
in credit to the SME sector, (ii) public sector banks to follow a transparent 
rating system with cost of credit linked to the credit rating of the enterprises, 
(iii) commercial banks to make concerted efforts to provide credit cover on an 
average to at least 5 new tiny, small and medium enterprises at each of their 
semi-urban/ urban branches per year, (iv) special dispensation under the 
Credit Guarantee Scheme for all (a) loans upto Rs. 2 lakh, (b) eligible women 
entrepreneurs and (c) eligible borrowers located in the North Eastern region 
(including Sikkim) and Jammu and Kashmir, (v) adoption of cluster-based 
approach by banks for SME financing.

Closure of SSI units 
2565. SHRI N.R. GOVINDARAJAR: Will the Minister of SMALL 
SCALE INDUSTRIES be pleased to state: 
(a) the major factors responsible for closure of small scale industrial units 
in different parts of the country; 
(b) the number of labourers rendered jobless due to its closure, 
category-wise along with steps taken to provide employment to these workers 
and technicians; 
(c) whether Government are aware that small scale industrialists are 
facing infrastructural/technical problems like Sales Tax, Income Tax, Electricity 
Boards, and State financial institutions; and 
212 

[15 December, 2005] RAJYA SABHA  
(d) if so, the details thereof along with the action taked by Government 
in this regard for smooth functioning of these units? 
THE MINISTER OF SMALL SCALE INDUSTRIES (SHRI 
MAHABIR PRASAD): (a) Though closure of a small scale industry (SSI) is 
dependent on the decision of the SSI concerned, some of the major factors 
responsible for closure of SSIs are fall in demand for specific products, 
change in technology, inadequacy of working capital, shortage of raw 
materials, marketing problems, lack  of competitiveness, management 
inadequacies, etc. 
(b) The date on the number of labourers rendered jobless due to 
closure of SSIs are not maintained  centrally. However, workers and 
technicians rendered jobless due to clos ure of SSI units can avail of the self-

order to solve the problems faced by SSI sector, relating to availability of 
credit, technology upgradation, infra structure and marketing facilities, the 
Central Government also implements a number of schemes/programmes to 
supplement these efforts.    . 
Disaster Management support system 
2566. SHRI C. RAMACHANDRAIAH: Will the PRIME MINISTER 
be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the Department of Space has evolved a 
space based disaster management support system; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
(c) whether this system had been put to use during the recent natural 
disasters in the country; and 
(d) if so, the extent of success achieved as a result of it? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE PRIME MINISTER'S OFFICE 
(SHRI PRITHVIRAJ CHAVAN): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. The 
213 

RAJYA SABHA [15 December, 2005] 
Space based disaster management supp ort system being implemented by 
Department of Space, jointly with Ministry of Home Affairs, comprises of 
the following elements: 
— Creation of digital database, for disaster-prone areas, towards 
facilitating hazard zonation and damage assessment; 
monitoring of major natural disasters using satellite and aerial 
data, and development of related techniques and tools. 
— Strengthening the communica tions backbone for timely 
dissemination of information and emergency support. 
— Setting up of a secure satellite based communication network 
linking the National Control Room at Ministry of Home Affairs 
with State Control Rooms and other concerned organizations. 
— Establishment of a Decision Support Centre at National Remote 
Sensing Agency (NRSA) of Department of Space, at Hyderabad, 
towards facilitating the disaster management operations by 
Ministry of Home Affairs. 
(c) and (d) Yes, Sir. The system had been put to use during the recent 
floods, tsunami, agricultural drought, earthquake, landslides and forest fires. 
Major flood events that occurred  during 2005 were monitored, 
mapped, and the information was furnished to the Ministry of Home affairs, 
Central Water Commission, and Relief Commissioner of the concerned 
States. The flood inundation information provided in near real time has been 
found to be useful for organizing relief operations and assessment of the 
damages. 
The artificial lake formed on the Pareechu River in the Tibetan region 
during July-August 2004, with threats of flash floods downstream in 
Himachal Pradesh, was monitored regularly till June 2005 and the 
information was provided to Ministry of Home Affairs for alert and 
necessary action. 
The post-tsunami relief, rehabilitati on and reconstruction efforts were 
supported by way of providing satellite phones for emergency 
214 

[15 December, 2005] RAJYA SABHA 
communication, enabling telemedicine facilities and videoconferencing for 
rescue of the displaced people, da mage assessment and development of 
integrated cadastral level information in selected areas. 
The damage assessment due to th e recent earthquake in Jammu & 
Kashmir in October 2005 was carried out, and information was sent to 
Ministry of Home Affairs for relief and rehabilitation activities. 
During the 2005 Kharif season, mild agricultural drought was observed 
in parts of Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Haryana, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan and 
Uttar Pradesh. The agricultural drought information was sent to Ministry of 
Agriculture and the concerned State Agriculture Departments towards 
planning relief and contingency measures. The drought information is being 
used regularly by Ministry of Agriculture and State Departments of 
Agriculture to pursue drought management activities. 
Forest fire information derived from satellite data, on regular basis, is 
disseminated through the web site of NRSA of Department of Space.

Disaster warning set up in States 
2569. SHRIMATI VANGA GEETHA: Will the Minister of OCEAN 
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) the role of the disaster warning set up in each State, so far; 
(b) the amount spent for the purpose especially in Andhra Pradesh; 
(c) whether Government had taken the assistance of foreign firms with 
regard to the latest system in the process;     , 
(d) if so, the details thereof; and 
(e) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE OF THE DEPARTMENT OF OCEAN 
DEVELOPMENT (SHRI KAPIL SIBAL): (a) and (b) The question appears to 
refer to the Early Warning System for Tsunami and Storm Surges in Indian 
Ocean. As far as the Tsunami Warning System is concerned the Government is 
setting up an Early Warning System for Tsunami and Storm Surges in Indian 
Ocean at the total cost of Rs. 125 Crores with the following components:— 
• strengthening of the existing seismological network to indicate, near 
real time occurrence of tsunamigenic earthquakes; 
• Installation of tsunami warning sensors close to the ocean-bottom at 
appropriate locales in the In dian Ocean, with real time 
connectivity; 
• Tide gauge and data buoys networking to validate arrival of tsunami 
waves at the coast; 
• Modelling of the inundation scenarios for the entire coast and 
mapping of potential risk areas; 
• Collection of information, analysis and generating status 
advisories. 
A Centre would be set up at Indian National Centre for Ocean 
Information Services (ICOIS), Hyderabad,  Andhra Pradesh on a 24x7 basis. 
The system is scheduled to be operationalised by September, 2007. The Tsunami 
Warning System is for the whole country. 
221 

RAJYA SABHA [15 December, 2005] 
(c) to (e) There is no assistance taken from foreign firms, however, the 
Indian system is the best system for our country.

last twenty years. Survey for construction of this line was completed in
